case_name: Pepsico India Holding Private Limited v Krishna Kant Pandey
respondent:
Krishna Kant Pandey
Supreme Court of India

6 January 2015
C.A. No. 28 of 2015 [Arising out of S.L.P. (C) No. 32616 of 2013] (Arising out of impugned final judgment and order Dt. 23/05/2013 in W.P. No. 102/2008 passed by the Allahabad High Court)
The Judgment was delivered by : M. Y. Eqbal, J.
1. Leave granted.
2. This appeal by special leave is directed against judgment and order dated 23.5.2013 of the High Court of Allahabad at Lucknow Bench whereby learned Single Judge classifying the respondent as 'workman' allowed the writ petition preferred by him, quashed the order dated August 24, 2007 passed by the Industrial Tribunal II, State of Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow (in short, 'the Tribunal') and directed the Tribunal to decide respondent's Case No.84/2004 on merit.

facts: The respondent was appointed on the post of Operator/Technician Grade III for six months on probation basis w.e.f. 13th of March, 1995 against the salary of Rs. 2600/- per month.
He was confirmed w.e.f. 13th September, 1995 and was also awarded one increment w.e.f. 1st of February, 1996.
The respondent was promoted to the post of Line Supervisor in the pay scale of Rs. 7716/- and thereafter to the post of Fleet Executive.
He was terminated by giving one month's salary in lieu of notice prior to termination on 14th of November, 2003.

The respondent preferred a reference before the Conciliation Officer, Lucknow alleging that he is a 'workman' within the meaning of the Uttar Pradesh Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act') and termination of his services by the Company is contrary to S. 6 of the Act.

The respondent moved the High Court by way of a writ petition challenging the order of the Tribunal and also for his re- instatement to the post of Fleet Executive with continuity of service and for payment of full back wages.
issues: Whether the respondent was a 'workman' within the meaning of the Uttar Pradesh Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
Whether the termination of the respondent's services by the Company is contrary to S. 6 of the Act.
petitioner_arguments: The High Court has exceeded its jurisdiction conferred upon it u/art. 226 of the Constitution of India by reversing the finding recorded by the Tribunal.
The High Court has committed grave error in issuing suo motu directions to the executive to amend a relevant provision of S. 2(z) of the U.P. Industrial Disputes Act (in short, 'State Act').
The High Court cannot mandate the executive to introduce or enact a legislation, howsoever necessary or desirable.

The High Court has failed to appreciate that the nature of duties and responsibilities entrusted upon the respondent are not manual, skilled or unskilled or technical services, but manual, managerial and supervisory.
respondent_arguments: Before conciliation, the appellant raised an objection with regard to the jurisdiction of the Tribunal and the matter was finally referred to the Labour Court for adjudication on a limited question as to whether the termination of services of the respondent was justified.
The Labour Court has limited jurisdiction to adjudicate the disputes referred to it and not to enter into any other question that may be raised in the reference.
court_reasoning: The admitted facts are that at the relevant time, the respondent was working as a Fleet Supervisor and drawing a salary of Rs. 7716/-.
The Labour Court recorded the evidence adduced by both the appellant and the respondent and discussed the evidence, and elaborately considered the case of the parties.
The Labour Court finally recorded finding that the respondent is not a workman within the meaning of S. 2(z) of the Act.
holding: The appeal is allowed and the order passed by the High Court is set aside. The reference made to the Labour Court is restored to its original position, i.e., whether the termination of services of the respondent was justified or not.
